n50641.head: ἰπνοκαής
n50641.html:
ἰπνοκαής, ές, (καίω)

baked in the oven, Luc. Lex. 6.

n50643.head: ἰπνοκήιον
n50643.html: ἰπνοκήιον φρύγιον, οἱ δὲ τὴν ὑπόκαυσιν τοῦ ἰπνοῦ, Hsch.

n50644.head: ἰπνολέβης
n50644.html:
ἰπνολέβης, ητος, ὁ,

boiler, cauldron, Luc. Lex. 8, Ath. 3.98c.

n50645.head: ἰπνολεβήτιον
n50645.html: ἰπνολεβήτιον, τό, Dim. of foreg., Poll. 10.66.

n50646.head: ἴπνον
n50646.html:
ἴπνον, τό,

mareʼs-tail, Hippuris vulgaris, Thphr. HP 4.10.1.

n50647.head: ἰπνοπλάθος
n50647.html:
ἰπνοπλάθος [ᾰ], ὁ, (πλάσσω)

oven-maker, fire-clay moulder, worker in terra-cotta, much like κοροπλάθος (q. v.), Pl. Tht. 147a:—later ἰπνοπλάθης, Poll. 7.163, Tim. Lex., Harp.:—also ἰπνο-πλάστης, ου, ὁ, Gal. Thras. 43:

n50649.head: ἰπνός
n50649.html:
ἰπνός, ὁ,

oven, furnace, Hdt. 5.92.ηʹ, Hp. Morb. 2.47, Antiph. 176.4, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath. 2.54a, Archestr. Fr. 46; esp. for heating water for the bath, Ar. V. 139, Av. 437 (ῐπν-).

II the place of the oven, i.e. the kitchen, Semon. 7.61, Ar. V. 837, Lycurg. Fr. 73.

III lantern, Ar. Pax 841, Pl. 815, SIG 1027.13 (Cos, iv/iii B.C.), Ael. NA 2.8.

IV = κοπρών, dunghill, privy, Ar. Fr. 353, Hsch. (Prob. cogn. with Engl. oven.)

corr.why: The century notation requires Roman iv/iii; current 1v substitutes an Arabic digit within the Roman numeral.

n50650.head: ἰπνών
n50650.html:
ἰπνών, ῶνος, ὁ,

kitchen, IG 11(2).287 A 147, al. (Delos, iii B.C.).

n50651.head: ἰποκτόνος
n50651.html:
ἰποκτόνος [ῑ], ον, (ἴψ)

killing the worms in vines, epith. of Heracles at Erythrae, Str. 13.1.64.

n50652.head: ἶπος
n50652.html:
ἶπος, ἡ (so in Pi. l.c.) or τό (Eust. 844.39), in a mouse-trap,

the piece of wood that falls and catches the mouse, Ar. Pl. (815?) ap. Poll. 10.155, Id. 7.41, Eust. 16.40, etc. cf. εἶπος.

2 any weight, fullerʼs press, Archil. 169; ἶ. ἀνεμόεσσα, of Aetna as the weight which holds Typhoeus down, Pi. O. 4.8; press used in surgery, Hp. Mochl. 38. (Perh. cf. ἴπτομαι.)

n50653.head: ἰπόω
n50653.html:
ἰπόω,

press, squeeze, Cratin. 91; esp. in surgery, Hp. Art. 47; ἰ. τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ βραχίονος Heliod. ap. Orib. 49.13.8:—Pass., to be weighed down, ἰπούμενος ῥίζαισιν Αἰτναίαις ὕπο A. Pr. 365; ἰπούμενος ταῖς ἐσφοραῖς Ar. Eq. 924.

n50654.head: ἴππα
n50654.html: ἴππα, ἡ, v. sub ἴπνη: as pr. n. Ἵππα, Hippa, nurse of Dionysus, Orph. H. 48.4.

n50655.head: ἱππαγρέται
n50655.html:
ἱππαγρέται, ῶν, οἱ, (ἀγρέω) three officers at Lacedaemon,

who chose 300, the flower of the ἔφηβοι, to serve as a body-guard for the kings (v. ἱππεύς II.1), X. HG 3.3.9, Lac. 4.3, Archyt. ap. Stob. 4.1.138: sg., Th. 4.38 (unless it be pr. n.).

n50656.head: ἵππαγρος
n50656.html:
ἵππαγρος, ὁ,

= ἵππος ἄγριος, wild horse, Opp. C. 3.252.

n50657.head: ἱππαγωγός
n50657.html:
ἱππαγωγός, όν,

carrying horses; esp. of ships used as cavalry transports, πλοῖα Hdt. 6.48; νέες ib. 95; ναῦς Th. 2.56, 4.42, Arr. An. 2.19.1; τριήρεις D. 4.16, D.S. 11.3; ἱππαγωγοί alone, Ar. Eq. 599, D. 4.21: Ἱππαγωγός as pr. n. of a ship, IG 2(2).1623.14.

n50658.head: ἱππάζομαι
n50658.html:
ἱππάζομαι, Dor. fut. 3 sg. ἱππασεῖται Dialex. 6.4:—

drive horses, drive a chariot, Ἀντίλοχʼ, ἀφραδέως ἱππάζεαι Il. 23.426; later, ride, Hdt. 4.114, Hp. Aër. 17, Ar. Nu. 15, etc.; ἱ. ἐφʼ ἵππων Hdt. 4.110; ἵππῳ X. Eq. 10.1: metaph., ἁ ξυσμὰ ἐκ ποδὸς εἰς κεφαλὰν ἱππάζεται Sophr. 53:—rare in Act., ἱππάσαι πῶλον ap. Poll. 1.182.

2 Pass., of the horse, to be ridden or driven, Pl. Ion 540e; to be broken in for riding, X. Eq. 3.1.

II c. acc. loci, ἱππάζεσθαι χώραν ride over a country, Plu. Cam. 23; τὰς ὁδούς D.S. 13.88.

n50659.head: ἱππαΐς
n50659.html:
ἱππαΐς, ΐδος, ἡ,

hyperdor. for ἱππηΐς, fem. of ἱππικός I.3, of a knight, πόρπα, i.e. fibula which fastened the trabea of a Roman eques, Epigr.Gr. 985.1 (Philae).

n50660.head: ἱππαιχμία
n50660.html:
ἱππαιχμία, ἡ,

cavalry-action, Sch. Pi. N. 1.23 (pl.).

n50661.head: ἵππαιχμος
n50661.html:
ἵππαιχμος, ον,

fighting on horseback, equestrian, Pi. N. 1.17.

n50662.head: ἱππάκη
n50662.html:
ἱππάκη [ᾰ], ἡ,

mareʼs-milk cheese, used by the Scythians, Hp. Aër. 18, A. Fr. 198, Theopomp.Hist. 48, Thphr. HP 9.13.2, Dsc. 2.71:—also ἱππάκης, ου, ὁ, Eust. 916.16.

2 horseʼs rennet, Dsc. 2.75.

II a leguminous plant, Ph. Bel. 86.25, Plin. HN 25.83.

n50663.head: ἱππακοντιστής
n50663.html:
ἱππακοντιστής, οῦ, ὁ,

mounted javelineer, Ael. Tact. 2.13, Arr. An. 4.4.7, Poll. 1.131.

n50664.head: ἱππάκοπον
n50664.html:
ἱππάκοπον, τό, (cf. ἄκοπος)

remedy for horses, Hippiatr. 130.

n50665.head: ἱππαλεκτρυών
n50665.html:
ἱππαλεκτρυών, όνος, ὁ,

horse-cock, gryphon, a fabulous animal in A. Fr. 134, cf. Ar. Ra. 932, Av. 800.

n50666.head: ἱππαλέος
n50666.html: ἱππαλέος, α, ον, poet. for ἱππικός, Opp. C. 1.169, 242, etc.

n50667.head: ἵππαλος
n50667.html:
ἵππαλος, ὁ,

name of the monsoon in the Indian Ocean (from the name of the pilot who observed it), prob. in Peripl.M.Rubr. 57.

n50668.head: ἱππαναβάτης
n50668.html:
ἱππαναβάτης [βᾰ], ου, ὁ,

mounted man, PLond. 1821.80.

n50669.head: ἱππάνθρωπος
n50669.html:
ἱππάνθρωπος, ὁ,

centaur, Gal. UP 3.1, Eust. 1909.53.

n50670.head: ἱππαπαῖ
n50670.html: ἱππαπαῖ, a cry of the Ἱππεῖς, a parody of the boatmenʼs cry (ῥυππαπαῖ), Ar. Eq. 602.

n50671.head: ἱππάριον
n50671.html:
ἱππάριον, τό,

Dim. of ἵππος, pony, PCair.Zen. 30, al. (iii B.C.), Arr. Tact. 19.3.

2 wretched horse, in contempt, X. Cyr. 1.4.19, Plu. Phil. 7, Them. Or. 24.306d.

3 statuette of a horse, IG 11(2).203B 84 (Delos, iii B.C.).

n50672.head: ἱππαρμοστής
n50672.html:
ἱππαρμοστής, οῦ, ὁ, Laced. for ἵππαρχος,

commander of cavalry, X. HG 4.4.10, 5.12; cf. ἵπφαρμος.

n50673.head: ἱππαρχεῖον
n50673.html:
ἱππαρχεῖον, τό,

head-quarters of the ἵππαρχος, IG 2(2).895 (ii B.C.).

n50674.head: ἱππαρχέω
n50674.html:
ἱππαρχέω,

to be ἵππαρχος, command cavalry, c. gen., τῆς ἵππου Hdt. 9.20, 69; ἱππαρχηκὼς ἀνδρῶν καλῶν κἀγαθῶν Din. 3.12; ἱππέων D. 21.164: abs., X. Ages. 2.4, Lys. 26.20, D. 21.172; οἱ ἱππαρχηκότες Hyp. Lyc. 17; of the Roman magister equitum and praefectus equitum, D.C. 43.48, App. BC 5.8:—Pass., serve under an ἵππαρχος, Arist. Pol. 1277b10.

n50675.head: ἱππάρχης
n50675.html:
ἱππάρχης, Dor. ἱππ-άρχας, Ion. gen. ἱππάρχεω IG 12(8).194.7 (Samothrace), Michel 596 (Cyzicus), ὁ,

= ἵππαρχος, OGI 217 (Caria, iii B.C., pl.), Plb. 10.22.6 (Achaean), 18.22.2 (Macedonian), cf. LXX 2 Ki. 1.6, PTeb. 54.2 (i B.C.), Plu. Tim. 32; at Sparta, IG 5(1).32A, al.; = Lat. magister equitum, Plb. 3.87.9, D.H. 5.75, Nic.Dam. 130.17J., etc.; = praefectus equitum, App. BC 2.102; = praefectus alae, J. BJ 2.14.5.

n50677.head: ἱππαρχία
n50677.html:
ἱππαρχία, ἡ,

office of ἵππαρχος, X. Ath. 1.3 (pl.); of the magister equitum, D.C. Fr. 36.26, Lyd. Mag. 2.13.

II a squadron of horse such as he commands, Plb. 10.23.4, D.S. 17.57, Str. 17.1.12, Plu. Eum. 7, Arr. An. 1.24.3; consisting of 512 men, Ascl. Tact. 7.11, etc.

n50678.head: ἱππαρχικός
n50678.html:
ἱππαρχικός, ή, όν,

of or for a ἵππαρχος, ἡγεμονία ἱ.,= ἱππαρχία, Suid. s.v. ἵππαρχος; ἱ. ἐστί it is part of his duty, X. Eq.Mag. 5.1: -ικός, ὁ (sc. λόγος), title of treatise by Xenophon.

n50679.head: ἵππαρχος
n50679.html:
ἵππαρχος, ὁ,

ruling the horse, epith. of Poseidon, Pi. P. 4.45.

II commander of cavalry, τῆς ἵππου Hdt. 7.154; at Athens, IG 2(2).116.15 (iv B.C.), Ar. Av. 799, Lys. 16.8, Pl. Lg. 755c, 880d, X. Eq.Mag. 1.7, al.; ἵ. εἰς Λῆμνον χειροτονεῖν Hyp. Lyc. 17, cf. D. 4.26; in other states, Th. 4.72, IG 7.2466 (Thebes, iii B.C.), etc.; in the Achaean league, ib. 5(2).344.7 (Orchomenus), etc.; = Lat. magister equitum, D.S. 12.64, Plu. Cam. 5, etc.; = praefectus equitum, App. Hisp. 47; cf. ἱππάρχης.

n50680.head: ἱππάς
n50680.html:
ἱππάς, άδος, ἡ, pecul.fem. of ἱππικός, ἱ. στολή

a riding-dress, Hdt. 1.80; = Lat. equester, ἱ. ἐσθής D.C. 38.14.

II as Subst., ἡ ἱ. (sc. τάξις) the order of knights (ἱππεῖς) at Athens, Arist. Pol. 1274a21; θυσίαι, βοῦς ἱππάδες of sacrifices offered by the knights, Hsch.; πύλαι ἱ., name of a gate at Athens, Plu. VOrat. 2.849c.

2 knights’ tax, ἱππάδα τελεῖν Is. 7.39, Arist. Ath. 7.4, Plu. Sol. 18; θητικοῦ ἀντὶ τέλους ἱππάδʼ ἀμειψάμενος Epigr. ap. Arist. Ath. l.c.

3 at Rome, = ordo equester, D.C. 40.57, al.; in full ἡ ἱ. τάξις Hdn. 5.1.5.

4 a boyʼs game, Poll. 9.122.

5 = ἵππος, ἡ, mare, Opp. C. 1.162, Hippiatr. 14, BGU 21iii 8 (iv A.D.).

n50681.head: ἱππασία
n50681.html:
ἱππασία, ἡ,

riding, horse-exercise, Ar. Ach. 1165 (lyr.); ἱ. ποιεῖσθαι,= ἱππάζεσθαι, to take a ride, X. Eq. 8.9, cf. An. 2.5.33; ἱ. ἱππάσασθαι Id. Oec. 11.17; horsemanship, Id. An. 2.5.33; as a subject of competition, IG 7.3087 (Lebad.).

2 chariot-driving, Luc. DDeor. 20[12].1, etc.

II cavalry, Arr. An. 4.4.7.

n50682.head: ἱππάσιμος
n50682.html:
ἱππάσιμος [ᾰ], η, ον,

fit for horses, fit for riding, Αἴγυπτον τὸ πρὶν ἐοῦσαν ἱππασίμην καὶ ἁμαξευομένην, opp. ἄνιππος, Hdt. 2.108, cf. 5.63, 9.13, X. Cyr. 1.4.14, Aen.Tact. 6.6, Plb. 10.49.5, Onos. 31.1, etc.; τὸ ἱππάσιμον, i.e. τὸ πεδινόν, X. HG 7.2.12; τὰ ἱ. τῆς χώρας ἄνιππα ποιεῖν Aen.Tact. 8.4: metaph., τοῖς κόλαξιν ἑαυτὸν ἀνεικὼς ἱππάσιμον allowing himself to be ridden by flatterers, Plu. Alex. 23.

n50683.head: ἱππάσιον
n50683.html: ἱππάσιον, τό, Dim. of ἵππος, Theognost. Can. 125.

n50684.head: ἵππασμα
n50684.html:
ἵππασμα, ατος, τό,

a ride, Ach.Tat. 1.13.

n50685.head: ἱππασμός
n50685.html:
ἱππασμός, ὁ,

riding, Sch. E. Hel. 1355.

n50686.head: ἱππαστήρ
n50686.html:
ἱππαστήρ, ῆρος, ὁ,

= sq. [ἱππαστής, = ἱππευτής, horseman], metaph. of the μύωψ, AP 5.202 (Asclep.); κημός ib. 7.424 (Antip. Sid.).

n50687.head: ἱππαστής
n50687.html:
ἱππαστής, οῦ, ὁ,

= ἱππευτής [horseman], Luc. Am. 46.

II as Adj., fit for riding, of a horse, X. Eq. 10.17.

n50688.head: ἱππαστί
n50688.html:
ἱππαστί, Adv.

like a horseman, καθίζειν Hsch.

n50689.head: ἱππαστικός
n50689.html:
ἱππαστικός, ή, όν,

fond of riding, Plu. Alc. 23.

n50690.head: ἱππαστός
n50690.html:
ἱππαστός, ή, όν,

that can be ridden, Arist. HA 576b17.

n50691.head: ἱππάστριαι
n50691.html:
ἱππάστριαι κάμηλοι, αἱ,

dromedaries, Plu. Eum. 15.

n50692.head: ἱππάφεσις
n50692.html:
ἱππάφεσις, εως, ἡ,

starting-post in a race-course, Plb. Fr. 52 (pl.), Abh.Berl.Akad. 1904(2).9 (Pap., ii B.C.), D.H. 3.68 (pl.), Epigr. ap. Paus. 6.20.14 (Olymp.), prob. in SIG 251H ii 63, 253 U (Delph., iv B.C.):—also ἱππάφια, τά, Tab.Defix.Aud. 234.21 (Carthage, i A.D.).

n50693.head: ἱππαφίδες
n50693.html:
ἱππαφίδες,

caballi ammissi, carceres, Gloss. (prob. -αφέσεις).

n50694.head: ἱππεία
n50694.html:
ἱππεία, ἡ, (ἱππεύω)

riding or driving of horses, horsemanship, racing, S. El. 505 (lyr.): pl., E. HF 374 (lyr.).

II cavalry, X. An. 5.6.8, Ages. 1.23.

III breed of horses, ἐνδόξου γενομένης ἐνθένδε ἱ. Str. 5.1.9.

n50695.head: ἵππειος
n50695.html:
ἵππειος, α, ον, (ἵππος)

of a horse or horses, ζυγόν, φάτνη, Il. 5.799, 10.568; κάπαι Od. 4.40; ἵ. λόφος horse-hair crest, Il. 15.537; ἔντεα Pi. N. 9.22; γένος, μάνδραι, S. Ant. 341 (lyr.), Fr. 659.3; ἔθειραι Theoc. 16.81; τὸ ἵππειον [γάλα] Arist. HA 522a28, Posidon. ap. Gal. 19.712; κάλω ἱππείω δύο IG 1(2).330.19. Adv. -είως Dam. Pr. 58.

2 ἵππειος, ὁ (sc. μήν), name of month at Thronion, Klio 16.176 (Delph.). (ἵππιος is the usual form in Trag., ἱππικός in Prose.)

n50697.head: ἱππελάτης
n50697.html:
ἱππελάτης [ᾰ], ου, ὁ,

driver or rider of horses, Opp. C. 1.95.

n50698.head: ἱππέλαφος
n50698.html:
ἱππέλαφος, ὁ, lit.,

horse-deer, perh. nylghau, Portax picta, Arist. HA 498b32; ἡ θήλεια ἱ. οὐκ ἔχει κέρατα ib. 499b2.

n50699.head: ἱππεραστής
n50699.html:
ἱππεραστής, οῦ, ὁ,

lover of horses, Ael. NA 2.28.

n50700.head: ἵππερος
n50700.html:
ἵππερος, ὁ,

horse-fever, formed after ἴκτερος, ὕδερος, etc., with a pun on ἔρος ( = ἔρως), Ar. Nu. 74.

n50701.head: ἵππευμα
n50701.html:
ἵππευμα, ατος, τό,

ride on horseback or journey in a chariot, E. IT 1428; [Νύξ], μακρὸν ἵ. διώκεις Id. Fr. 114 (lyr.).

n50702.head: ἱππεύς
n50702.html:
ἱππεύς, gen. έως (-έω dub. in Hsch.), Ep. ῆος, ὁ, (ἵππος)

one who fights from a chariot, Hom. (only in Il.), opp. πεζός, 2.810; either of the driver or of the hero who fights, 12.66, 15.270; also of one who drives in a chariot-race, 23.262.

2 horseman, rider, cavalryman, ἰππήων στρότος Sapph. Supp. 5.1, cf. Hdt. 3.88, 9.49, A. Pers. 14 (anap.), Arist. Pol. 1270a29, etc.; τῆς πολιτείας ἱ. a public courier, Aristaenet. 1.26.

3 groom, Class.Rev. 27.12 (Laodicea Combusta), 24.12, JHS 18.108 (near Lysias).

II ἱππεῖς, in social and political sense, knights, forming an aristocracy in early Greek communities, Arist. Pol. 1297b18, etc.; at Eretria, ib. 1306a35, Ath. 15.2; at Sparta, a royal bodyguard, Hdt. 8.124, cf. 1.67, etc.; esp. at Athens, the Second Class in Solonʼs constitution, Arist. Ath. 7.3; later, an aristocratic corps of cavalry, Ar. Eq. 225, And. 3.5, Philoch. 100, etc.

2 of the Roman equites, D.S. 37.8, D.H. 4.24, App. BC 1.22, etc.; ἱππεὺς Ῥωμαίων,= Lat. eques Romanus, Mon.Anc.Gr. 7.17, IG 3.768a, IGRom. 3.204 (Ancyra), OGI 547.2 (ibid.), 645.7 (Palmyra), prob. in IGRom. 4.1213 (Thyatira).

III nimble kind of crab, Arist. HA 525b8.

IV kind of comet, Plin. HN 2.90, Lyd. Ost. 11.

V girlʼs ornament, Hsch., cf. Ostr. 323 (ii B.C.).

VI a measure, πυρῶν, ἀμυγδάλων, ἀλεύρων, Supp.Epigr. 2.710 (Pednelissus).

n50703.head: ἵππευσις
n50703.html:
ἵππευσις, εως, ἡ,

riding, in pl., Sch. E. Ph. 791.

n50704.head: ἱππευτήρ
n50704.html:
ἱππευτήρ, ῆρος, ὁ,

= sq., πῶλος, ἱ. πεδίων, οὐχ ἁλός AP 9.295 (Bianor).

n50705.head: ἱππευτής
n50705.html:
ἱππευτής, οῦ, ὁ,

rider, horseman, Pi. P. 9.123: as Adj., Τρῶες B. 12.160; στρατός E. HF 408 (lyr.).

n50706.head: ἱππεύω
n50706.html:
ἱππεύω,

to be a horseman or rider, ride, Hdt. 1.136, etc.; ἱ. ταῖς κυούσαις ἵπποις Arist. HA 576a21; ἱ. ἐπʼ ὄνου Luc. Bacch. 2; of a people, ἱππεύει ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη Hdt. 7.84, cf. 87:—also in Med., Id. 1.27, 79.

2 metaph., of the wind, ζεφύρου πνοαῖς ἱππεύσαντος E. Ph. 212 (lyr.); σελάνα ἱππεύουσα διʼ ὀρφναίας Id. Supp. 994 (lyr.); also, rush, πρὸς φόνον Id. HF 1001.

II serve in the cavalry, Lys. 14.7, X. HG 3.1.4, Pl. Lg. 756b, etc.

2 at Rome, to be an eques, D.C. 49.12; τὸ -εῦον the ordo equester, Id. 60.7.

III of a horse, as we say ‘the horse rides (i.e. carries his rider) well’, X. Eq. 1.6, 3.4, 10.3.

IV drive a team, Ar. Nu. 1406.

n50707.head: ἱππηγέτης
n50707.html:
ἱππηγέτης, ου, ὁ,

driver of horses, of Poseidon, Lyc. 767.

n50708.head: ἱππηγός
n50708.html:
ἱππηγός, όν, (ἄγω)

= ἱππαγωγός, νῆες (expressed or understood) Philoch. 132, Plb. 1.27.9, D.S. 20.83; τριήρης Ἱππηγός as pr. n., IG 2(2).1628.423,1629.944.

n50709.head: ἱππηδόν
n50709.html:
ἱππηδόν, Adv.

like a horse, A. Th. 328 (lyr.), Supp. 431 (lyr.).

II like a horseman, Ar. Pax 81.

n50710.head: ἱππηλασία
n50710.html:
ἱππηλασία, ἡ, (ἐλαύνω)

driving or riding of horses, Hld. 8.14, Them. Or. 15.188a, 18.216d:—Adj. ἱππ-ηλάσιος, α, ον, fit for riding or driving, ἱ. ὁδός chariot-road, Il. 7.340.

n50712.head: ἱππηλάτης
n50712.html:
ἱππηλάτης, ου, ὁ,

driver of horses, one who fights from a chariot, Hom. (always in Ep. from ἱππηλάτα, and only in nom.), as an epith. of honour, Knight, ἱ. Τυδεύς, γέρων ἱ. Πηλεύς, Φοῖνιξ, Οἰνεύς, Il. 4.387, 7.125, 9.432, 581; Νέστωρ Od. 3.436: generally ἱππηλάται E. Rh. 117: as Adj., ἱ. λεώς, opp. πεδοστιβής, A. Pers. 126 (lyr.).

n50713.head: ἱππήλατος
n50713.html:
ἱππήλατος, ον,

fit for horsemanship or driving, νῆσος Od. 4.607; γαῖα 13.242; ὁδὸς ἱ. chariot-road, Luc. Rh.Pr. 3, Poll. 9.37; ἱ. οἶδμα Nonn. D. 20.157; θάλασσα Agath. 4.29, cf. 5.11; ἱ. ἔργον Ἀθήνης, i.e. the Trojan horse, Tryph. 2; τὸ διʼ ἡδονῆς καθάπερ ἱ. τι χωρίον Porph. Marc. 6.

n50714.head: ἱππημολγία
n50714.html:
ἱππημολγία, ἡ,

milking of mares, Scymn. 855 (pl.).

n50715.head: ἱππημολγοί
n50715.html:
ἱππημολγοί, οἱ, (ἀμέλγω)

the Mare-milkers, a Scythian or Tartar tribe, Il. 13.5, cf. Str. 7.3.2; Σκύθαι ἱ. Hes. Cat.Oxy. 1358Fr. 2.15; ἱ. Κιμμέριοι Call. Dian. 252.

corr.why: The tribal plural requires the masculine article οἱ. Current οι loses its rough breathing and is incorrectly presented as an inflection.

n50717.head: ἱππιάναξ
n50717.html:
ἱππιάναξ [ᾰν], ακτος, ὁ,

king of horsemen, A. Pers. 996 (lyr.).

n50718.head: ἱππίας
n50718.html:
ἱππίας, ου, ὁ,

= ἱππεύς IV, Apul. ap. Lyd. Mens. 4.7.

n50719a.head: ἱππιατρικός
n50719a.html:
ἱππιατρικός, ή, όν,

of or for farriery: ἱππιατρικόν, τό, a work on farriery, Suid. s.v. Χείρων: -κά, τά, title of extant compilation: also -κόν, τό, tax on farriers, PHib. 1.45.21 (iii B.C.).

n50719.head: ἱππιατρός
n50719.html:
ἱππιατρός (on the accent v. Hdn. Gr. 1.229), ὁ,

veterinary surgeon, farrier, IG 9(2).69.5 (ii B.C.), PGen. 42.35 (iii A.D.), Hippiatr. 12, etc.; cf. ἱπποϊατρός:—Adj.

n50720.head: ἱππίδιον
n50720.html:
ἱππίδιον, τό,

a kind of fish, Epich. 44.

n50721.head: ἱππικός
n50721.html:
ἱππικός, ή, όν, (ἵππος)

of a horse or horses, freq. in Trag., ἱ. ἐκ πλευμόνων A. Th. 61; ἱ. φρυάγματα ib. 245, cf. S. El. 717, 719; ὀχήματα, ἄντυγες, ib. 740, Aj. 1030; φάτναι E. Ba. 509.

2 of horsemen or chariots, ἀγών Hdt. 1.167, And. 4.26 (pl.); in ἱππικῶν ἀγών S. El. 698, ἱππικῶν is prob. neut. (v. infr. IV); δρόμος ib. 754; ναυάγια ib. 730; ἆθλον Pl. Lg. 949a.

3 = Lat. equester, τάξις, ἀξίωμα, D.H. 12.1, Plu. Pomp. 23; of persons, of equestrian rank, ἱ. ἄνδρες Str. 3.4.20, cf. IGRom. 3.474 (Lycia, iii A.D.), etc.

II of riding or horsemanship, equestrian, X. HG 5.3.20; ἱ. ἄσκησις training in horsemanship, IG 2(2).1042.21, al.; ἱ. ἡγήτωρ leader of the knights, ib. 3.693; skilled in riding, opp. ἄφιππος, Pl. Prt. 350a, al.: Comp., Satyr. 1, Phld. Mus. p.6 K.: Sup., Arr. Tact. 16.9.

2 ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη), horsemanship, riding, Ar. Nu. 27, etc.; περὶ -κῆς, title of treatise by Xenophon; ἱ. ἐπιστήμη Pl. La. 193b; ἱ. λόγοι X. HG 5.3.20; τὰ ἱ. [πράγματα] Pl. Alc. 1.124e, cf. Thg. 126a; ἡ ἐμὴ ἱ. this riding of mine, Lys. 24.10.

III fit for riding, Sup. -ώτατον, χρῆμα γυνή Ar. Lys. 677.

IV τὸ ἱ. the horse, cavalry, Hdt. 7.87, E. Supp. 682, X. An. 6.5.29, etc.; τὰ ἱ. Plb. 3.114.5.

2 course or space of four stadia, Plu. Sol. 23.

b the circus at Rome, Tab.Defix.Aud. 187.59.

V Adv. -κῶς like a horseman: Sup. -κώτατα with best horsemanship, X. Oec. 21.7.

n50722.head: ἵππιος
n50722.html:
ἵππιος, α, ον, (ἵππος) poet. form of ἵππειος (q. v.),

of a horse or horses, λόφοι crests of horsehair, Alc. 15.2; σθένος ἵ. Pi. P. 2.12; Ἄργος ἵ. (cf. ἱππόβοτος) Id. I. 7(6).11, B. 18.15; δρομεύς, prob. l. in E. El. 825; ἄνασσα ἱ. Queen of the Amazons, Id. Hipp. 307; epith. of Poseidon as creator of the horse, B. 16.99, A. Th. 130 (lyr.), Ar. Eq. 551, Nu. 83, IG 1(2).310.142, etc.; hence, of Colonos as sacred to him, Arg. S. OC, Paus. 1.30.4 (but cf. Pherecr. 134); also of Athena, Pi. O. 13.82, S. OC 1070 (lyr.), Harp.; of Hera, at Olympia, Paus. 5.15.5; of Ares, Id. 5.15.6, cf. Tryph. 105.

II of horsemen or the horse-race, ἵ. νόμος Pi. O. 1.101; ἱππίαν ἔσοδον Id. P. 6.50; ἄεθλα AP 6.312 (Anyte); sc. ἀγών SIG 1064.8 (Halic., i B.C.).

III Ἵππιος, ὁ (sc. μήν), month at Rhegium, IG 14.612.

n50723.head: ἱππιοχαίτης
n50723.html:
ἱππιοχαίτης, ου, ὁ,

shaggy with horsehair, λόφος Il. 6.469.

n50724.head: ἱππιοχάρμης
n50724.html:
ἱππιοχάρμης, ου, ὁ,

one who fights from a chariot, 24.257, Od. 11.259, Hes. Fr. 7; later, horseman, rider, A. Pers. 29 (anap.).

II as Adj., ἱ. κλόνοι the tumult of the horse-fight, ib. 105; cf. ἱπποχάρμης.

n50725.head: ἱππίσκος
n50725.html:
ἱππίσκος, ὁ, Dim. of ἵππος, name of a play by Alexis, Ath. 3.120b.

2 small statue of a horse, Michel 832.41 (Samos, iv B.C.).

II an ornament for the head (cf. ἱππεύς v), Cratin.Jun. 5, Hsch.

n50726.head: ἱππιστί
n50726.html:
ἱππιστί, Adv.,

= ἱππηδόν, astride, Ἀφροδίτη ἱ. καθημένη ἐπὶ Ψυχῆς PMag.Par. 1.1724.

n50728.head: Ἱππιών
n50728.html: Ἱππιών, ῶνος, ὁ (sc. μήν), month at Eretria, IG 11 (4).1066b21 (found in Delos).

n50729.head: ἱπποβάμων
n50729.html:
ἱπποβάμων [ᾱ], ον, gen. ονος, (βαίνω)

going on horseback, equestrian, Ἀριμασπὸν ἱπποβάμονα στρατόν A. Pr. 805; στρατὸς ἱ., of centaurs, S. Tr. 1095.

2 trotting like a horse, or used for riding, κάμηλοι A. Supp. 284 (cj. Turneb.).

3 metaph., ῥήματα ἱ. high-paced words, bombast, fustian, Ar. Ra. 821.

n50730.head: ἱπποβάτης
n50730.html:
ἱπποβάτης [ᾰ], ου, ὁ,

horseman, A. Pers. 26 (anap.).

II ἱ. ἵππος or ὄνος, stallion, Str. 8.8.1, Hippiatr. 14; cf. ἱπποβότης.

n50731.head: Ἱππόβινος
n50731.html: Ἱππόβινος, ὁ, (βινέω) comic distortion of the pr. n. Ἱππόνικος,= ἱππόπορνος, Ar. Ra. 433.

n50732.head: ἱπποβόσιον
n50732.html:
ἱπποβόσιον, τό,

horses’ keep, Theognost. Can. 125.

n50733.head: ἱπποβοσκός
n50733.html:
ἱπποβοσκός, όν, (βόσκω)

feeding horses, Ael. NA 6.10, Suid., Gloss.

n50734.head: ἱπποβότης
n50734.html:
ἱπποβότης, ου, ὁ, (βόσκω)

feeder of horses, Ἀτρεύς E. Or. 1000 (lyr., but prob. -βώτα), IA 1059 (but prob. -βάτας).

II ἱπποβόται, οἱ, at Chalcis in Euboea a social class (cf. ἱππεύς II), Knights, Hdt. 5.77, 6.100; ἡ ἱπποβοτῶν πολιτεία Arist. Fr. 603.

n50735.head: ἱππόβοτος
n50735.html:
ἱππόβοτος, ον, (βόσκω)

grazed by horses, Od. 4.606, E. Andr. 1229 (anap.), IG 1(2).1034, Just. Nov. 25.1; ἡ ἱ., at Chalcis, Ael. VH 6.1 (cf. foreg.); esp. of the plain of Argos, from the rich pastures of Lerna, Il. 2.287, al., B. 10.80, E. Supp. 365 (lyr.).

n50736.head: ἱπποβουκόλος
n50736.html:
ἱπποβουκόλος, ὁ,

horse-herd, horse-keeper, S. Fr. 1057, E. Ph. 28.

n50737.head: ἱππόβροτοι
n50737.html:
ἱππόβροτοι ὠδῖνες pangs that gave birth

to a horse and man (Pegasus and Chrysaor), Lyc. 842.

n50739.head: ἱππογνώμων
n50739.html:
ἱππογνώμων, ον, gen. ονος,

judging well of horses: hence generally, quick in judging, τινος A. Fr. 243, cf. Hsch.
